title: Prove the exact 744-call F3 optimum for full ternary five-source demand
body:
## Summary

For the unsigned F3 complete-call connector of #4225 with five immutable sources and one arbitrarily dirty restored connector, I replace the 31 binary-mask rows with **all 242 nonzero ternary coefficient rows**. The exact optimum is **744 calls**, three above the 741-call operator-count floor. This answers #4225's second open question. The claim type is a **scoped proof backed by an exhaustive finite census**. There is no new κ and no selected-frontier change. Only `research/f3-ternary-demand-connector/` is added.

- **Lower bound.** #4225's mod-three count argument puts every operator count in 3ℤ, each at least 3. A word below 744 must therefore sit exactly at 741, with a 15-event path and three readouts per row. That holds iff the triple sums of the path's boundary vectors cover F3^5 \ {0}. I enumerated all 1,401,400 such paths up to source relabeling. The maximum coverage is **241** (30 paths, each missing one row), so no 741-call word exists.
- **Two 744-call constructions.** (a) An 18-event path that uses one source six times covers all 242 rows with three readouts each. (b) A 15-event path covers 241 rows, and the missing row (1,2,0,1,2) takes six readouts.
- **Tariff.** For arbitrary positive source prices c_j and one common readout price α, the exact bill is `3Σc_j + 726α + 3·min(min_j c_j, α)`.
- **Other source counts.** The floor `3n + 3(3^n − 1)` is attained for n = 1..4 (canonical census). It fails at n = 5 (this result), and fails by counting for every n ≥ 7. n = 6 is open.

## Evidence and reproduction

The verifier uses only the standard library and writes no files. It runs the census and checks the canonical reduction against full labeled enumeration at n = 2, 3. It checks six literal 744-call words (five relabeled doubled-source words and one gap word) in two ways: a generic noncommuting coefficient ledger, and dense random F3 execution at L = 2, 3 with dirty registers. It also runs five rejection controls and four tariff fixtures. A positive control confirms that #4225's binary path covers 203 ternary rows.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/f3-ternary-demand-connector/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f3-ternary-demand-connector
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/f3-ternary-demand-connector --check-source-history
```

Expected marker: `PASS_F3_TERNARY_DEMAND_CONNECTOR calls=744 rows=242`. All three pass locally. Each registered command (normal and `-O`, warnings as errors) takes about 37–38 s, dominated by the census. An independent C enumeration I wrote during development, not committed, gave the same canonical count and maximum.

## Limitations

- This is the abstract unsigned complete-call interface over F3 only.
- Fixed prices must include complete primitive implementations. Admission, coefficient preparation, dispatch of the 744-record word and physical charges are additional and unknown.
- The exact envelope for row-dependent readout prices is **not** claimed. It needs every minimal missing set, and only the lone gaps are recorded.
- For n ≥ 7 only the lower bound (floor + 3) is proved, not the exact optimum.
- No consumer for ternary demand is identified.
- No proof-kernel certificate exists, and the selected cold replay was not run. This is not a complete multiplication theorem.

## Open next questions

1. The exact envelope for unequal readout prices: compute the inclusion-minimal missing sets of all 15-event paths.
2. Six sources: is the 2202-call floor attained? This needs a compiled census of 190,590,400 canonical paths, or one reduced by rotation and reversal symmetry.
3. A concrete caller that needs coefficient-2 rows.

## Related open work

- #4225 (head `397025101d23195a5193c7912e6cd384eccdbf1c`): binary-mask predecessor, with the same interface and count floor. Its 15-event path is used here as a control: it covers 203 of 242 ternary rows, checked numerically. Its 108-call binary optimum is a different demand.
- #4232 (head `86ad339efc9f817846479431d8cc0f04edf95fb9`): binary-mask floor for every source count. Its n = 5 value of 108 is consistent with binary attainment, while ternary demand fails at n = 5. The demand families differ, and no number overlaps.
- #4231: unsigned five-source binary-mask connector across characteristics. It is a different demand, with no overlapping ternary number.
- #4189: one-source unsigned F3 result (binary row only). Ternary one-source demand has two rows and attains its 9-call floor here.

Fresh overlap included the 100 most recent open PR titles, recent account PRs, the last 30 handoff comments, `find_overlap.py` for `connector-alphabet-change` and a PR title search for "ternary". Closed work and arbitrary diffs are incompletely covered.

## CI notes

All hosted checks passed in [run 39488529668](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39488529668): `plan` (2m39s) and the package `replay` (4m17s, both registered commands). No failed job or unrun registered check remains.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. The blast radius is one new isolated package and its opt-in replay.
